topic: Bayes' Theorem and Independence: Unlocking Predictive Logic

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly define conditional probability P(A|B) as 'the probability of A given that B has already occurred.' Use a Venn diagram animation to show the 'shrinking' sample space from the full area to just the region of B.
sections.example: Visualizing a bag of marbles: If you know the marble drawn is red (Event B), how does that change the probability it came from Box 1 (Event A)?

sections.title: Defining Independence
sections.content: Define independence as a state where knowing Event B gives no information about Event A. Mathematically: P(A|B) = P(A). Use a graphic showing two independent coins: one outcome does not move the needle on the other's probability.
sections.example: Flipping a coin (Event A) and rolling a die (Event B). The outcome of the coin does not change the probability distribution of the die.

sections.title: Bayes' Theorem: The Logic of Reversal
sections.content: Introduce Bayes' Theorem as a bridge between P(A|B) and P(B|A). Present the formula: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B). Use an animated flow chart showing the 'Prior' probability being updated by 'Evidence' to reach a 'Posterior' probability.
sections.example: A 'Medical Diagnostic' scenario: A character (Dr. Owl) wants to know the probability a patient has a rare disease (A) given they tested positive (B), considering the test's accuracy (P(B|A)).

sections.title: Synthesis and Practical Application
sections.content: Summarize how independence simplifies Bayes' Theorem (if events are independent, the theorem collapses). Conclude with a visual 'Decision Tree' that demonstrates how Bayesian updating works in AI and machine learning systems.
sections.example: A spam filter bot: Using Bayes' Theorem to calculate the probability an email is 'Spam' (A) based on the presence of specific keywords (B), updating the filter's certainty over time.
